**What this workbook is for.** Microsoft has notified subscription owners that, starting **31 July 2026**, Azure applies **capacity growth restrictions** to older-generation (v1–v4) virtual-machine series. On the impacted series you can no longer create **new deployments**, **scale out** for more capacity, or get **quota increases** approved. Existing VMs keep running on already-approved quota — but you cannot grow. Some of these series also **retire on 31 July 2028**, after which the VMs stop working.

**What this page shows.** A live count (from Azure Resource Graph) of every VM in your selected subscriptions that runs on an impacted series, broken down by **SKU version**, **subscription**, and **region**. Two impact levels are colour-coded:
- 🔴 **Retiring 2028 + capacity restricted** — plan migration; these disappear on 31 Jul 2028.
- 🟠 **Growth-controlled (v3/v4)** — no retirement date yet, but you cannot add capacity or quota.

**How to use it.** Use the filters above (subscription, region, size, family, version) to narrow the scope, review the charts and the exportable table below, then open the other tabs: **Affected VMs** (every VM to act on), **Migration Plan** (what to move each series to), **Capacity Risk** (which subscriptions are blocked from growing), and **Guidance & Resources** (official steps and links). Every grid can be exported with the **⤓ Export to Excel** button on its toolbar."},"name":"text - overview intro"},{"type":1,"content":{"json":"### Impacted VMs at a glance"},"name":"text - ov glance"},{"type":3,"content":{"version":"KqlItem/1.0","query":"Resources

**The notification in plain terms.** Azure is restricting growth on older v1–v4 VM series so it can invest in newer hardware. From **31 July 2026**, on the impacted series you cannot: deploy new VMs, scale out for more capacity, or get quota increases approved. **Already-approved quota and existing VMs are unaffected** — they keep running. Some series also **retire on 31 July 2028** and stop working after that date.

### Impacted — set to retire in 2028 (capacity restricted now)
- **Compute optimized:** F, Fs, Fsv2
- **General purpose:** D, Ds, Dv2, Dsv2, Av2, Amv2, B, Bs
- **Memory optimized:** G, Gs
- **Storage optimized:** Ls, Lsv2

### Impacted — subject to growth controls (v3 / v4)
- **General purpose:** Dv3, Dsv3, Dv4, Dsv4, Ddv4, Ddsv4, Dav4, Dasv4
- **Memory optimized:** Ev3, Esv3, Ev4, Esv4, Edv4, Edsv4, Eav4, Easv4

### Recommended newer-generation series
- **General purpose:** Dv5, Dv6, Dv7 (or Dl / Dd variants)
- **Memory intensive:** Ev5, Ev6, Ev7 (or Ed variants)

### Required actions — before 31 July 2028
1. **Review** current usage of v1–v4 VMs across your subscriptions — the **Overview** and **Affected VMs** tabs do this for you.
2. **Plan and migrate** workloads to newer-generation VM series (resize the VM, or redeploy on a new size).
3. **Confirm** workloads function as expected after migration.

### Official resources
- [Legacy VM size series capacity limitations and migration guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/migration/sizes/legacy-series-capacity-limitations)
- [Migration guidance for newer-generation VM series (v6/v7)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/migration/sizes/sizes-v6-v7-migration-overview)
- [Retired VM sizes migration guide (D / Ds / Dv2 / Dsv2 / Ls)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/lifecycle/retirement/d-ds-dv2-dsv2-ls-series-migration-guide)
- [Change the size of a virtual machine](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/resize-vm?tabs=portal)
- [Select a disk type for Azure IaaS VMs (managed disks)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/disks-types)
- [VM pricing calculator](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/calculator/)

_Source: Azure service notification "Capacity growth restrictions for older generation v1–v4 Azure VM series." Recommended replacement sizes are guidance — validate each target against your workload using the migration guides above._
